title: Free Resources Directory for Seniors
subtitle: Free benefits, tech classes, legal aid, health information, and discounts for seniors — grouped by category, official links only.
credits: Published by Asdale Dynamics, LLC (Indiana, formed Oct 2026). Beginner-friendly AI education, books, and practical tools.

categories.label: Benefits & assistance
categories.description: Government benefits and aid programs seniors may qualify for.

categories.label: Tech classes
categories.description: Free technology classes and digital literacy help for seniors.

categories.label: Legal aid
categories.description: Free or low-cost legal help and information for older adults.

categories.label: Health info
categories.description: Free, trustworthy health information for seniors and caregivers.

categories.label: Discounts & savings
categories.description: Senior discounts and savings programs — free to look up.

resources.name: Social Security — Retirement & SSI Benefits
resources.costDetail: Free to apply; benefit amounts depend on work history and income
resources.description: Retirement benefits, disability benefits, and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) for seniors and people with limited income.
resources.whoItHelps: Workers 62+, people with disabilities, and low-income seniors (SSI)
resources.howToAccess: Create a free my Social Security account at ssa.gov to apply, check your statement, and manage benefits.

resources.name: Medicare
resources.costDetail: Free to enroll; some parts have premiums based on income
resources.description: Federal health insurance for people 65 and older, and younger people with disabilities.
resources.whoItHelps: Adults 65+ and people with qualifying disabilities
resources.howToAccess: Visit medicare.gov to learn about Part A, Part B, Part D, Medicare Advantage, and enrollment periods.

resources.name: Medicaid
resources.costDetail: Free or low-cost health coverage based on income and state rules
resources.description: Health coverage for low-income adults, including seniors who qualify based on income and assets.
resources.whoItHelps: Low-income seniors and people with limited resources
resources.howToAccess: Apply through your state Medicaid agency or HealthCare.gov; medicaid.gov has state-by-state information.

resources.name: Benefits.gov — Benefit Finder
resources.costDetail: Free to use; no account required to browse
resources.description: Official U.S. government benefits questionnaire that matches you to programs you may qualify for.
resources.whoItHelps: Anyone looking for federal and state benefits
resources.howToAccess: Answer a few questions at benefits.gov to get a personalized list of benefit programs.

resources.name: Eldercare Locator (Area Agency on Aging)
resources.costDetail: Free service; call or search online
resources.description: Connects older adults and caregivers to local services — transportation, meals, caregiving, and benefits counseling — through your Area Agency on Aging.
resources.whoItHelps: Seniors, caregivers, and family members
resources.howToAccess: Search by ZIP code at eldercare.acl.gov or call 1-800-677-1116.

resources.name: SNAP (Food Assistance)
resources.costDetail: Free to apply; benefits issued monthly on an EBT card
resources.description: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program helps low-income seniors buy groceries.
resources.whoItHelps: Low-income seniors and households
resources.howToAccess: Apply through your state SNAP office; fns.usda.gov/snap explains eligibility and how to apply.

resources.name: LIHEAP (Energy Bill Assistance)
resources.costDetail: Free to apply; helps pay heating and cooling bills
resources.description: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program helps eligible households pay home energy bills.
resources.whoItHelps: Low-income seniors and households with high energy costs
resources.howToAccess: Apply through your state LIHEAP office; benefits.gov/liheap has details.

resources.name: VA Benefits for Veterans
resources.costDetail: Free to apply; some services have copays based on priority group
resources.description: Health care, disability compensation, pension, and burial benefits for veterans and their families.
resources.whoItHelps: Veterans, service members, and eligible family members
resources.howToAccess: Apply at va.gov or visit your local VA medical center or Vet Center.

resources.name: Senior Planet (AARP) — Free Tech Classes
resources.costDetail: Free online and in-person tech classes; no AARP membership required for many classes
resources.description: Free technology classes, workshops, and coaching designed for older adults — smartphones, video calling, online safety, and more.
resources.whoItHelps: Seniors learning to use technology
resources.howToAccess: Browse the class calendar at seniorplanet.org and register online.

resources.name: GCFGlobal — Free Tech Tutorials
resources.costDetail: Completely free; no account needed
resources.description: Free tutorials on computers, email, internet basics, smartphones, and everyday tech skills, written in plain language.
resources.whoItHelps: Beginners of any age learning technology
resources.howToAccess: Go to gcfglobal.org and pick a topic — no sign-up required.

resources.name: DigitalLearn (Public Library Association)
resources.costDetail: Free courses; no library card required to browse
resources.description: Short, beginner-friendly courses on computer basics, internet safety, job skills, and more from the Public Library Association.
resources.whoItHelps: Adults new to computers and the internet
resources.howToAccess: Start a course at digitallearn.org — no account required to begin.

resources.name: AARP TEK Workshops & Virtual Community Center
resources.costDetail: Free workshops; some events open to non-members
resources.description: Free technology workshops and online events for seniors on devices, apps, and staying connected.
resources.whoItHelps: Seniors and caregivers
resources.howToAccess: Find upcoming workshops at aarp.org/tek or the AARP Virtual Community Center.

resources.name: Legal Services Corporation — Find Legal Aid
resources.costDetail: Free or low-cost civil legal help for eligible clients
resources.description: Federally funded civil legal aid. Use the locator to find a legal aid office near you.
resources.whoItHelps: Low-income seniors and households
resources.howToAccess: Use the Find Legal Aid tool at lsc.gov to locate your nearest legal aid office.

resources.name: LawHelp.org — Free Legal Help Directory
resources.costDetail: Free to search; connects to free and low-cost legal aid
resources.description: State-by-state directory of free legal aid offices, self-help resources, and legal information.
resources.whoItHelps: People needing free or low-cost legal help
resources.howToAccess: Select your state at lawhelp.org to find local legal aid and self-help guides.

resources.name: Pro Bono Net
resources.costDetail: Free to use
resources.description: Connects people to volunteer lawyers and free legal resources, including tools for seniors.
resources.whoItHelps: People who cannot afford a lawyer
resources.howToAccess: Search for free legal help and self-help tools at probono.net.

resources.name: National Elder Law Foundation
resources.costDetail: Free directory; lawyer consultation fees vary
resources.description: Certifies elder and special needs law attorneys. Use the directory to find a qualified elder law attorney near you.
resources.whoItHelps: Seniors and families planning for aging
resources.howToAccess: Search the certified attorney directory at nelf.org.

resources.name: MedlinePlus (NIH)
resources.costDetail: Completely free; no ads
resources.description: Trustworthy, easy-to-read health information from the National Library of Medicine — conditions, drugs, and wellness for seniors.
resources.whoItHelps: Seniors, caregivers, and anyone seeking health info
resources.howToAccess: Search conditions, medicines, and healthy aging topics at medlineplus.gov.

resources.name: National Institute on Aging (NIH)
resources.costDetail: Free publications and online info
resources.description: Free health information on aging, Alzheimer's, caregiving, exercise, and healthy living for older adults.
resources.whoItHelps: Older adults and caregivers
resources.howToAccess: Order free publications or read online at nia.nih.gov/health.

resources.name: CDC — Healthy Aging & Preventive Health
resources.costDetail: Free public health information
resources.description: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention guidance on vaccines, screenings, fall prevention, and healthy aging.
resources.whoItHelps: Seniors and caregivers
resources.howToAccess: Visit cdc.gov/aging for vaccines, screening schedules, and fall-prevention tips.

resources.name: HealthCare.gov — Marketplace & Medicaid
resources.costDetail: Free to browse and apply; plan costs vary by income
resources.description: Official health insurance marketplace where you can compare plans and check Medicaid/CHIP eligibility.
resources.whoItHelps: People shopping for health insurance, including early retirees
resources.howToAccess: Apply or browse plans at healthcare.gov during Open Enrollment or a Special Enrollment Period.

resources.name: AARP Member Discounts & Advantages
resources.costDetail: Directory is free; AARP membership required to use most discounts
resources.description: Member-only discounts on travel, dining, shopping, health, and entertainment.
resources.whoItHelps: AARP members (age 50+)
resources.howToAccess: Browse the discount directory at aarp.org/advantages.

resources.name: National Park Service Senior Pass
resources.costDetail: Low one-time fee ($20 annual or $80 lifetime); entry to many parks is free with the pass
resources.description: America the Beautiful Senior Pass for U.S. citizens and permanent residents 62+, providing entry to national parks and federal recreation sites.
resources.whoItHelps: Seniors 62+ who visit national parks
resources.howToAccess: Buy online at store.usgs.gov/pass or in person at a participating park.

resources.name: Amtrak Senior Discount
resources.costDetail: Free to qualify; 10% off most fares for seniors 65+
resources.description: 10% discount on most Amtrak fares for passengers 65 and older.
resources.whoItHelps: Train travelers 65+
resources.howToAccess: Book at amtrak.com and select the senior discount; proof of age may be required.

resources.name: Retail Senior Discounts (Official Store Policies)
resources.costDetail: Free to ask; discounts vary by store and location
resources.description: Many grocery, pharmacy, and retail chains offer senior discount days or everyday savings — check each store's official policy.
resources.whoItHelps: Seniors shopping at participating stores
resources.howToAccess: Ask customer service at your local store or check the store's official website for senior discount days.
